Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

system noun

a method, an organised whole

also method, scheme, the system

classical

Cic. Fam. 1.8.4: commūtāta tōta ratiō est
Cic. Off. 3.20: Stōicōrum ratiō disciplīnaque (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 195, 335

ratiō, ratiōnis f.

noun, third declension

a system, a method; an order worked out by reason

Lewis & Short: order, system; a theory or doctrine; a method. A judicial system, ratiō jūdiciālis (Traupman 195).

Other words

  • disciplīna, disciplīnae f. — a system of teaching or doctrine; a way of doing things

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Cato Agr. 1.4: aliēnam disciplīnam; Cic. Off. 3.20 (Lewis & Short)

  • ōrdō, ōrdinis m. — order, arrangement

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Col. 12.2.4: dispositiōne atque ōrdine

  • systēma, systēmatis n. — a whole made of parts; a technical system

    noun, third declension · also used · late Latin · Mart. Cap. 9.947 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 53, 261

    Greek σύστημα; in Latin only late (Martianus Capella). Traupman uses it for a stereo system and a computer’s operating system.

Examples

  • commūtāta tōta ratiō est senātūs, jūdiciōrum, reī tōtīus pūblicae

    the whole system has changed: the senate, the courts, the entire stateCic. Fam. 1.8.4

  • cavētō aliēnam disciplīnam temere contemnās

    take care not to scorn someone else’s system rashlyCato Agr. 1.4

See also policy, government.
